SEC
    SBC rows_m1
    BCS last_cell
    EOR #&FF
    TAX                             \ the rows after this cell, less 1: kept in X (neither loop touches it), stored only if needed below
.byte
    LDA (v_ptr),Y
    STA (s_ptr),Y
    DEY
    BPL byte
    LDA s_ptr                       \ the next cell: the screen a character row up (C = 0 from
    SBC #&7F                        \ cell's SBC: this takes &80)...
    STA s_ptr
    LDA s_ptr + 1
    SBC #&02                        \ (high &40-&7F: no borrow, C = 1 after)
    ORA #&40                        \ ...round the 16K (&3D-&3F to &7D-&7F; no AND: the draw's rule, as .draw_column's)
    STA s_ptr + 1
    LDA v_ptr                       \ ...the save block 8 on (C = 1: ADC #7 adds 8)
    ADC #7
    STA v_ptr
    LDY #7
    BCC g0a9b_e_test
    INC v_ptr + 1
.g0a9b_e_test                       \ Y = 7, X = rows_m1 (the rows after the cell just done, less 1)
    CPX #8
    BCC part_byte                   \ under 8: the last cell (the hot path)
    TXA                             \ the column goes on: this cell is whole, 8 rows (C = 1 from the CPX)
    SBC #8
    TAX
    CLC                             \ as the full test leaves it for the byte loop
    BRA byte                        \ 65C02 opcode
.last_cell                          \ rows_m1 = Y - the last line: rows_m1 + 1 bytes to put back
    LDX rows_m1                     \ (X is free in columns: .more reloads it)
.part_byte
    LDA (v_ptr),Y
    STA (s_ptr),Y
    DEY
    DEX
    BPL part_byte
    BRA columns                     \ 65C02 opcode
candidates.summary: Best (C, A and D overlap it: alternatives). The rows-after-this-cell count stays in X from the first cell (EOR #&FF / TAX, no STA rows_m1; neither byte loop touches X), so the next cell, nearly always the last, is tested with CPX #8 / BCC part_byte instead of TYA / SEC / SBC rows_m1 / BCS last_cell / LDX rows_m1 (Y is already 7 there): 8 cycles for 16. A column that goes on (rows >= 8, about 1 next cell in 7) does X -= 8 (TXA / SBC #8 / TAX, C = 1 from the CPX), CLC, BRA byte. A column ending in its first cell (BCS last_cell) loads rows_m1 as before. Also AND #&3F dropped (redundant, as draw_column) and JMP columns -> BRA columns (in range, same 3 cycles). Measured (pcprof on the bench build, 2026-10-22): render 23430 -> 23373 a pass on seed 1, 28406 -> 28323 holding RIGHT; passlock seed 1 3000 passes with screen, and helilock flight 5, identical. 5 bytes larger: .compiled and all after slide up 5 (bench .compiled &9E8A -> &9E8F; the DEBUG_FULLREDRAW build keeps 2 bytes of room under its &B400 ASSERT, the gameplay build 55).
candidates.equivalence: Next cell, old: X dead after .more's TAX, flags dead, Y = 7 from LDY #7. Old test: 7 - rows_m1 >= 0 (C) iff rows_m1 <= 7 iff CPX #8 leaves C clear. Last cell: copies rows_m1 + 1 bytes from Y = 7 down with X = rows_m1, the value the first cell computed (EOR #&FF of Y - rows_m1 is the A the old STA stored and the new TAX copies). Not last (rows_m1 >= 8): the old generic path computed EOR #&FF of (7 - rows_m1) = rows_m1 - 8, stored it, and ran the byte loop with Y = 7 and C = 0 (BCS not taken); new: X = rows_m1 - 8 (SBC with C = 1 from the CPX, no borrow), CLC, the same byte loop with Y = 7: the same bytes copied, the same next-cell code with C = 0, and X holding the new count. First cell: unchanged but TAX replaces STA rows_m1 (rows_m1 in memory is then stale; its only readers are the generic last_cell, reached from the first cell's BCS after .more just stored it, and .cell's own SBC, entered only from .more's flow where .more stored it). v_ptr's carry path: INC v_ptr + 1 falls into the same test. ORA #&40 alone equals AND #&3F / ORA #&40 on &3D-&7D (bit 6 already set for &40-&7D; for &3D-&3F the ORA gives &7D-&7F). Exits: BRA columns replaces JMP columns; X and Y are dead on both (.more and the callers reload them).
candidates.relies_on: s_ptr+1 in &40-&7F (draw_column's ring); Y <= 7 at .cell; X untouched by both byte loops and the next-cell code (it is); rows_m1 not read after a column's first cell except by last_cell; BRA columns in range (-113 bytes) and in the same page as its target (&9E8x -> &9E1A bench; gameplay and fullredraw listings checked too). Page crossings: none of the window's branches cross (everything in one page: &9E bench/ship, &9C gameplay); the 5-byte slide of .compiled and everything after is measured only in the bench build (inside the totals above). rows_m1 (&CB) is renderer scratch: nothing reads it after .columns returns (.more rewrites it for the next column; render_zp's save/restore list does not include &CB; no interrupt touches it), so its final value differing is harmless. Only the window's own labels byte/cell/last_cell/part_byte are involved (cell: entered only by the fall-through from .cells_on_page and by the window; last_cell: only the window's BCS; no entry past a label: grep 'last_cell *+', 'part_byte *+', 'cell *+' finds none). s_ptr+1 is &40-&7F on entry (the record's byte 10 is written only by draw_column, line 1743, from its ring-wrapped s_ptr+1) and stays there, so AND #&3F is redundant: draw_column's own next-cell code already uses ORA #&40 alone (line 1801).
